newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS BEAT EAGLES, KNOCK PEETE OUT WITH INJURY.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS BEAT EAGLES, KNOCK PEETE OUT WITH INJURY.

text.p: Suddenly the Dallas Cowboys are looking very much alive while the Philadelphia Eagles, after the loss of quarterback Rodney Peete and a 23-19 defeat on Monday night, could be the ones in trouble.
The Dallas defence was the difference, capped by George Teague's interception near his own goal line in the final two minutes of regulation to kill a potential go-ahead drive.
The Eagles had the ball at the Dallas 30 when Ty Detmer threw a pass across the middle that Teague picked off and returned 20 yards yards.

Dallas ran three plays and punter John Jett intentionally ran out of the end zone with eight seconds left to cap the scoring. The Eagles returned the free kick to their own 30 but backup quarterback Bobby Hoying fumbled before he could get off a desperation pass.
Dallas intercepted two passes, recovered three fumbles and recored six sacks.

"I was really proud of the effort that our football team displayed tonight," said Dallas coach Barry Switzer. "It seemed like the guys were ready to play and they had great intensity and great emotion."
Detmer, who replaced Peete late in the second quarter, was 7-of-14 for 118 yards.

Peete was lost, probably for the season, after suffering a torn patella tendon in his right knee after catching his cleats in the turf. Philadelphia (3-2) fell one game behind the Washington Redskins for the lead in the NFC East.
"I'm disappointed because we had an opportunity to get something done and we didn't," said Eagles coach Ray Rhodes.
"There were a lot of things that happened during the course of the game. There's the possibility that Rodney is lost for the season.
"Ty Detmer came in the game and took a serious hit and he was a little fuzzy during the time he was in the game. That put us in a tough situation as far as trying to get some things executed.
"This is probably the toughest loss that we've gone through at home and, believe me, there's a lot of hurt behind that."
Troy Aikman was 13-of-23 for 149 yards and a touchdown for Dallas, which improved to 2-3 and avoided falling into the divisional basement in the absence of several stars.

"It was a huge game for us no doubt about it," Aikman said. "But it was as big a game as we made it. There was a lot of talk all week and I don't put any stock into that. I never understood that it shouldn't mean anything.
"We're world champions until somebody beats us. We were able to get our running game going. We were able to make the big plays. That was lacking before."
Wide receiver Michael Irvin sat out the final game of his five-game suspension and two-way player Deion Sanders had three receptions for 55 yards.
Philadelphia started out by building a 10-0 lead. Gary Anderson's 46-yard field goal 5:13 into the first quarter moved him into a tie with Eddie Murray for fourth place on the all-time points list.
Ricky Watters scored on a two-yard run to increase Philadelphia's lead to 10-0 with 3:48 left in the first.

Aikman found tight end Eric Bjornson with a five-yard scoring pass to pull the Cowboys within 10-7 with seven seconds left in the first quarter. Former Eagle Herschel Walker, who is in his second stint with the Cowboys, returned the kickoff to the Philadelphia 44.

Emmitt Smith's five-yard run capped a nine-play, 96-yard drive and gave the Cowboys the lead for good, 14-10, with 6:32 left in the second. Smith ran for 92 yards on 22 carries and had three receptions for 30 yards.

Sanders picked off a pass from Detmer and gave a lateral to Teague who returned it to the Philadelphia 34. After a pair of runs by Smith and an incomplete pass by Aikman, Chris Boniol kicked a 46-yard field goal to give the Cowboys a 17-10 lead.

Boniol's 30-yarder with 13 seconds left in the second quarter gave Dallas a 20-10 lead at the half. On the play that Peete injured his knee, Broderick Thomas recovered the fumble at the Philadelphia 30 to set up the field goal.
Rhett Hall picked off a pass from Aikman and returned it 32 yards to pull the Eagles within 20-17 just over a minute into the third.
The Eagles were again hurt by a turnover as Leon Lett recovered Detmer's fumble at the Philadelphia 34. Eight plays later, Boniol's 21-yarder gave the Cowboys a 23-17 lead.
